name: Drakon-Hollow
description: Drakon-Hollow is a graveyard that looks like a landscape: forests of petrified trees stand in dunes of yellow dust, some trunks thirty meters through, their stone grain so fine that saw-teams once mistook them for carved pillars. Canyon systems cut the dusty plateaus into labyrinths, and in their walls the strata record a wet green world that ended—by the rocks' account—in less than a century.

The thin air moans across the canyon rims at dusk, and by day the light is hard white and merciless; shadows are blue-black pools you could fall into. At night the temperature falls a hundred and eighty degrees and the silence has weight. Sand gets into everything, singing as it moves.

The petrified forests died standing: no toppled trunks, no burn layer, just stone where wood was, root systems intact in ground that dried around them. The Ashfall Consortium's failed terraforming program planted its atmospheric processors along the canyon rims forty years ago; the machines ran three years, then stopped in one night, diagnostics clean—and the colonists of New Sable walked out into the dust the same season, leaving meals on tables. Their tracks lead into the deepest canyon and stop at an unexcavated wall of dressed stone.

Silicon and hydrocarbons make Drakon-Hollow a mining prize regardless of its mood, and the charter reopens to new bidders this year. But core samples from beneath the stone forest keep returning carbon arranged in cellular patterns—modern, not fossil—and the processors' last logged instruction set was never written by anyone on the colony manifest.
